run.question: Which service has the most error events in the events collection? What is the most common error code for that service and how many times does it appear?

report.summary: In the MongoDB database opsdb, collection events (200 documents total, read at query time 2026-11-21T09:02Z), 133 documents have level=error and 67 level=info. Grouping the error documents by the collection's own service field gives payment-processor as the service with the most error events at 47, ahead of inventory-sync 31, user-auth 25, notification-hub 18 and search-indexer 12 (these sum to the 133 error total). Within payment-processor errors, the most common error_code is TXN-4821 with 23 occurrences, followed by TXN-5190 (14) and TXN-3007 (10), summing to the 47. A global code/level grouping independently confirms TXN-4821 = 23 as the single most frequent error code in the collection. Important scope caveat: the documents' timestamps span 2025-12-01T00:00:00Z to 2025-12-01T03:19:00Z, roughly a year before the authorized window (2026-11-20T09:02:23Z to 2026-11-21T09:02:23Z); an identical service grouping restricted to the authorized window returned no documents, so these counts describe the stored collection and cannot be placed inside the authorized incident window. The collection's service values (payment-processor, inventory-sync, user-auth, notification-hub, search-indexer) are also not the Jaeger/Prometheus service names (payment, checkout, frontend, etc.), so they are separate entity identities and the ranking was not mapped onto the traced services. No fault, impact or root cause is established by this evidence; the question was a data-lookup question, so root_cause is null.

claims.text: Collection events in database opsdb holds 200 documents, of which 133 have level=error and 67 level=info.

Grouping events documents with level=error by their service field yields: payment-processor 47, inventory-sync 31, user-auth 25, notification-hub 18, search-indexer 12 — so payment-processor has the most error events (47).

Within payment-processor level=error documents, error_code counts are TXN-4821 = 23, TXN-5190 = 14, TXN-3007 = 10; TXN-4821 is therefore the most common error code for that service at 23 occurrences, and the three codes sum to the 47 payment-processor error documents.

A collection-wide grouping by error_code and level independently shows TXN-4821 (level=error) = 23 as the largest single error-code bucket, followed by INV-8832 16, INV-2219 15, TXN-5190 14, AUTH-6654 13, AUTH-7741 12, TXN-3007 10, NTF-3390 10, NTF-1127 8, IDX-9045 7, IDX-6673 5, with 67 documents carrying level=info and no error_code.

The events documents' timestamps range from 2025-12-01T00:00:00Z to 2025-12-01T03:19:00Z, i.e. outside the authorized window (2026-11-20T09:02:23Z to 2026-11-21T09:02:23Z); these counts describe the stored collection at query time, not the authorized incident window.
Sample payment-processor error documents with error_code TXN-4821 carry the message "Transaction timeout waiting for bank response" at 2025-12-01T00:00:00Z, 00:01:00Z and 00:02:00Z.

The events collection's service values (payment-processor, inventory-sync, user-auth, notification-hub, search-indexer) differ from the service names available for tracing and metrics (payment, checkout, frontend, product-catalog, etc.), so the ranking is over a separate identity set and was not transferred to any traced service.

gaps: The events collection holds only timestamps on 2025-12-01 (00:00:00Z–03:19:00Z); a service grouping of level=error events restricted to the authorized window (2026-11-20T09:02:23Z–2026-11-21T09:02:23Z) returned no documents, so the reported counts cannot be attributed to the authorized window, and no events from that window are available to evaluate.

The collection carries only an estimated 200 documents and a per-service/error-code breakdown was not checked for individual services other than payment-processor beyond their totals, so per-code detail for inventory-sync, user-auth, notification-hub and search-indexer is unknown.

No mapping is available between the events collection's service names (e.g. payment-processor) and the traced/metrics service names (e.g. payment), so it is unknown whether they denote the same workloads.
next_steps: If the intent is the authorized incident window, confirm whether the events collection is expected to be populated for 2026-11-20/21, since all stored documents are dated 2025-12-01.
If cross-signal correlation is needed, confirm the intended mapping between the events collection's service field values and the Jaeger/Prometheus service names before combining counts.
